key_insight: The paper focuses on making EEG-derived features more consistently comparable for ADHD classification in children and adolescents. It curates 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions; the supplied abstract is incomplete and does not report classification results.
problem_solved: Differences in EEG preparation, analysis windows and recording-quality decisions can make feature comparisons unreliable.
method: Curate existing BALLADEER EEG data spanning 156 participants and five task conditions.
Use consistent signal preparation and shared analysis windows to support feature comparison.
Document recording-quality decisions to make the evaluation process transparent.
impact: Consistent EEG processing can help AI/ML practitioners compare candidate features more fairly and build more reproducible ADHD-classification evaluations. No accuracy gains or clinical benefits can be established from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Dataset overview: 669 recordings → 156 participants → five task conditions.
Processing pipeline: EEG recordings → consistent preparation → shared windows → feature comparison.
Five task-condition panels illustrating the dataset's experimental coverage.
Quality-control checklist highlighting documented recording decisions.
paper_title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
paper_authors: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco, Tahar Kechadi, Juan Trujillo
